'''Pierre van Moerbeke''' (born 1 October 1944 in [[Leuven]], [[Belgium]]) is a retired Belgian mathematician. He studies non-linear [[differential equation]]s and [[partial differential equation]]s, with [[soliton]] behavior. The [[Volterra lattice]], also called the Kac-van Moerbeke lattice, is named for him.<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Gesztesy | first1 = F.
 | last2 = Holden | first2 = H.
 | last3 = Simon | first3 = B.
 | last4 = Zhao | first4 = Z.
 | doi = 10.2307/2154302
 | issue = 2
 | journal = Transactions of the American Mathematical Society
 | mr = 1153014
 | pages = 849–868
 | title = On the Toda and Kac-van Moerbeke systems
 | volume = 339
 | year = 1993}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Van Moerbeke studied mathematics at the [[Catholic University of Leuven (1834–1968)|Catholic University of Leuven]], where he received his degree in 1966. He then obtained a PhD in mathematics at [[Rockefeller University]], [[New York City]] (1972). Formerly a professor of mathematics at [[Brandeis University]] ([[United States]]) and the Catholic University of Leuven,<ref name=francqui>{{citation|url=https://www.francquifoundation.be/wp-content/uploads/Rapport-Jury-van-Moerbeke_en.pdf|publisher=Fondation Francqui-Stichting|title=Ceremony of the Francqui Prize|date=June 3, 1988|access-date=2024-07-10}}</ref> he has retired to become a [[professor emeritus]] at Brandeis.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.brandeis.edu/mathematics/people/index.html|title=Faculty|work=Department of Mathematics|publisher=Brandeis University|access-date=2024-07-10}}</ref>

==Recognition==
In 1988, he was awarded the [[Francqui Prize]] on Exact Sciences.<ref name=francqui/>
